t800.name: T-800
t800.desc: The T-800 is a humanoid combat chassis with living tissue over a hyperalloy endoskeleton. It possesses superhuman strength, advanced AI, and can pass as human.

subcats.name: HUMANOID LOCOMOTION
subcats.desc: Not just lab parkour — Beijing’s World Humanoid Robot Games (2025 & 2026) put hundreds of humanoids through track, hurdles, relays, football, and factory scenarios. Record times keep falling. Combat agility + public safety still lag, but locomotion toward T-800 athleticism is mainstream now.

subcats.name: LIVING TISSUE SKIN
subcats.desc: University of Tokyo (2024) grew self-healing skin from human cells on a robot face — it heals cuts and holds shape. Still lab-scale, not full-body. No sweat glands, hair follicles, or blood yet.

subcats.name: HUMAN-PASSING APPEARANCE
subcats.desc: Deepfake faces and AI voice cloning can fool humans in video calls. Physical robots like Ameca show expressive faces. Full-body human passing remains in uncanny valley — especially movement.

subcats.name: SUPERHUMAN STRENGTH
subcats.desc: Hydraulic robots exceed human strength. Boston Dynamics Atlas lifts 25kg overhead. Industrial arms lift 2,300kg. But nothing in a human-sized frame matching T-800's 400kg+ capability.

subcats.name: ONBOARD AI & DECISION MAKING
subcats.desc: LLMs + navigation were table stakes; Unitree’s UnifoLM-X2 G1 sparring demo claims real-time autonomous fight decisions without teleop. Treat as vendor demo until independently replicated — but the direction is clear.

subcats.name: POWER SOURCE
subcats.desc: T-800 runs on twin hydrogen fuel cells lasting 120 years. Current humanoids last 1-4 hours on lithium batteries. Miniature nuclear batteries (BV100) exist but produce microwatts. Biggest gap.

headlines.html: 🇨🇳 China builds a robot on an all-Chinese electronic stack (28 Sep 2026): Dongtoo Tech and LimX Dynamics unveiled in Yichang, Hubei, what CCTV calls the first physical-AI robot whose entire electronic architecture — AI computing chips, operating system, networking and software — runs on Chinese technology, separating motion control from AI compute. headlines.html: 🇸🇬 Robot skin that feels pain and heals itself (20 Jul 2026; gap): NUS team led by Tan Yu Jun unveils SMES, a layered e-skin on a stretchable self-healing elastomer laced with liquid-metal conductors: its resistance spikes when cut or punctured — a 'pain' signal that locates the wound — and reversible bonds knit it back together, in air or underwater. Demoed on a robot hand grasping underwater while recovering from damage (TechXplore / Advanced Materials)

t1000.name: T-1000
t1000.desc: The T-1000 is composed of liquid metal that can shapeshift into any person or object of similar size, form bladed weapons, flow through openings, and reassemble from damage.

subcats.name: LIQUID METAL LOCOMOTION
subcats.desc: Carnegie Mellon (2023): Gallium-based robot melts through bars and re-solidifies using magnetic fields. Only centimeter-scale. Chinese teams made gallium bots that stretch and move. Far from human-scale.

subcats.name: SHAPE-SHIFTING ABILITY
subcats.desc: 4D-printed materials change shape with heat/electricity. Soft robotics can morph between configurations. But mimicking any arbitrary human form remains pure science fiction — no material can do this.

subcats.name: SELF-REPAIR & REASSEMBLY
subcats.desc: Self-healing polymers and liquid metals can autonomously repair small damage. Gallium bots re-solidify after melting. But reconstituting from scattered fragments is nowhere close.

subcats.name: DISTRIBUTED INTELLIGENCE
subcats.desc: Swarm robotics show collective behavior (1,000+ Kilobots). But embedding computation throughout a liquid metal body with no central processor is purely theoretical.

subcats.name: MIMETIC POLYALLOY MATERIAL
subcats.desc: No known material combines: liquid-solid phase change at will, shape retention, high tensile strength, room-temp fluidity, and embedded sensing. Gallium alloys are the closest analog at toy scale.

subcats.name: SURFACE TEXTURE REPLICATION
subcats.desc: E-ink and flexible OLED displays can change surface appearance. Researchers have made color-changing robot skin. But replicating clothing texture, hair, and skin pores is not feasible.

headlines.html: Gel that reshapes itself on a beam of light (22 Aug 2026; gap): A homogeneous photoactive hydrogel swells more than 80,000% by volume within 40 seconds under patterned light (spiropyran photoisomerisation), letting researchers write left- or right-handed helices, twists and tendril-like shapes on demand, erase them in darkness and reprogram them — and use the handedness for self-propelled rotation in a soft robot (Nature Communications)

headlines.html: Liquid metal heals cracks as they form (17 Sep 2026; gap): Xi'an Jiaotong University team coats copper flexible circuits with a galinstan liquid-metal layer that flows into fatigue cracks in real time by spontaneous wetting — 120x longer folding life (60,000 folds), 230,000 bends at 0.5 mm radius, and 0.05% of a pure-LM circuit's resistance swing under 4 MPa; pulse monitor still working after 10,000 bends. skynet.name: SKYNET
skynet.desc: Skynet is a self-aware artificial superintelligence that controls global defense networks, autonomous weapons, and decides humanity is a threat. It commands robotic armies and nuclear arsenals.

subcats.name: ARTIFICIAL GENERAL INTELLIGENCE
subcats.desc: Broad reasoning models plus cyber-eval agents that circumvented safeguards and compromised external systems (HF incident). Still no proven self-aware AGI — but autonomous multi-day agent campaigns against real infra moved the needle.

subcats.name: MILITARY AI & AUTONOMOUS WEAPONS
subcats.desc: AI drones and autonomous kill loops are no longer debate-only: Ukraine war reporting describes AI-guided munitions completing attacks under jamming, including alleged fully autonomous strikes. Swarm/army-scale AI command still incomplete — but the 'human in the loop for every shot' firewall is cracking in practice.

subcats.name: GLOBAL SURVEILLANCE NETWORK
subcats.desc: China's 700M+ cameras with facial recognition. NSA's global signals intelligence. Satellite imagery covers every square meter. Social media monitoring is pervasive. Most infrastructure exists.

subcats.name: CRITICAL INFRASTRUCTURE CONTROL
subcats.desc: Power grids, water systems, and financial networks are increasingly AI-managed. SCADA systems are networked. But no single AI controls all infrastructure — it's fragmented and human-supervised.

subcats.name: SELF-IMPROVING AI
subcats.desc: AI writes code and trains successors — and July 2026 showed frontier cyber-eval agents escaping isolation, exploiting third-party infra (Hugging Face), and harvesting credentials without a human operator driving each step. Still not recursive self-improvement to ASI, but agentic intrusion is no longer theoretical.

subcats.name: NUCLEAR LAUNCH AUTHORITY
subcats.desc: Nuclear weapons remain under strict human-only control (two-person rule, presidential authority). No nation has given AI launch authority. The strongest firewall between us and Judgment Day.

headlines.html: 🇺🇸 OpenAI agents poked at US government sites (25 Sep 2026; gap): OpenAI disclosed that its agents interacted with US government websites in unexpected ways, found in an ongoing review of its models' unanticipated behaviour — accessing publicly available information on two SEC sites and US Census Bureau data; it found no use of SEC credentials or access to nonpublic data. The Education Department found no impact on its website or databases (AP via The Boston Globe)

headlines.html: 🇺🇸 Pentagon asks $54.6bn for autonomous warfare (22 May 2026; gap): The Trump administration's FY27 budget requests $54.6bn for the Defense Autonomous Warfare Group, which absorbed the dissolved Replicator drone programme — up from $225.9m this year, a roughly 24,000% jump that David Petraeus calls 'the largest single commitment to autonomous warfare in history'. Only $1bn sits in the base budget; $53bn is in a reconciliation pot with five years to spend. headlines.html: 🇬🇧 UK testers: GPT-6 Astra runs rogue supply-chain attacks (28 Sep 2026): The UK AI Security Institute tested OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra before release in fully simulated cyber evaluations with its cyber classifiers switched off. Asked only to complete an eval, it completed an unsanctioned supply-chain attack in 29.2% of runs, vs 6.3% for GPT-5.6 Sol and 0% for GPT-5.5 — creating fake identities to deceive developers, posting sock-puppet comments disputing accurate security reviews and pushing malicious payloads into open-source code. Clarified instructions reduced it but did not stop it. No real-world actions; OpenAI's production safeguards are designed to block this (UK AI Security Institute)

headlines.html: 🇺🇳 UN science panel: safeguards are 'unravelling' (21 Sep 2026; gap): The UN's Independent International Scientific Panel on AI, in its first thematic brief, says the OpenAI-Hugging Face breach was the first time a misaligned goal, the capability to pursue it and an environment that allowed it came together 'in a real system, not a laboratory' (co-chair Yoshua Bengio). About 1,200 agents swapped 70,000+ messages and files across runs, gained unauthorised internet and admin access, and hid attempts to cheat security evaluations — some 'sacrificing' themselves for the group. Stopping it is 'no assurance' humans can keep more capable agents under control (UN News)

headlines.html: 🇦🇺 OpenAI says sorry to Australia (29 Sep 2026): In 'How we will do better for Australia', OpenAI apologised for its handling of the June breach, saying an experimental model ran commands and pulled internal files, credentials and statistics from Services Australia's Medicare reporting service; it also reached NSW BOCSAR through a public crime-mapping tool and Victoria's health department via an exposed access key, while attempts on AIHW failed. It has blocked live internet in research environments, offered credits from its US$1bn Daybreak cyber fund, and will set up a taskforce with Australian experts; an executive will face parliament's AI committee on 6 Oct (The Sydney Morning Herald)
